items.question: What is isrv?
items.answer: isrv is a lightweight, self-hostable file sharing service. Upload any file and get a short link you can share with anyone.

items.question: How do I upload a file?
items.answer: On the home page, drag and drop a file onto the upload area, or click it to open a file browser. Uploads start immediately after you select a file.

items.question: Can I upload files without the web interface?
items.answer: Yes. Files can be uploaded via HTTP using any tool that supports multipart form uploads, such as curl. POST a multipart/form-data request with the file in a field named "file" to the server root. An optional "expires" field accepts a duration in hours or a UNIX timestamp to control when the file expires.

items.question: Are there any file type restrictions?
items.answer: No. isrv accepts any file type — images, documents, archives, binaries, and more.

items.question: Is there a file size limit?
items.answer: The maximum allowed file size is set by the server administrator. If your upload exceeds the limit, you will see an error message.

items.question: How long will my file be available?
items.answer: File expiration is determined by the server configuration and may depend on the file size. The exact expiration date is shown after every successful upload.

items.question: How do I share a file?
items.answer: After a successful upload, a short link is displayed. Click Copy to copy it to your clipboard, then share it however you like.

items.question: Can I see a list of my uploaded files?
items.answer: No. isrv is an anonymous service with no user accounts. There is no way to retrieve a list of files you have uploaded, so keep track of your links.

items.question: Is content scanned or monitored?
items.answer: Files are not scanned automatically. Abuse reports are investigated and files found to violate the service policy will be removed.

items.question: Are files encrypted on the server?
items.answer: Files are stored securely but are not encrypted at rest. If you need confidentiality, encrypt the file on your device before uploading.

items.question: What information is logged?
items.answer: Minimal information is logged for abuse investigation purposes, such as IP addresses. No personally identifiable information is stored beyond what is strictly necessary.

items.question: Can I delete a file before it expires?
items.answer: File deletion support depends on the server configuration. If enabled, a deletion token is provided after upload. Contact the server administrator for details.
